event.ione_heart2.0.text: Oh, [player]! Come here. The oldest almanac in the room has been keeping something from me.
event.ione_heart2.0.why: the almanac becomes a character; a library with secrets, said lightly

event.ione_heart2.1.text: A chart of the coast. Hand-drawn, every cove, and the ink nearly gone. Somebody loved this shore precisely.
event.ione_heart2.1.why: 'precisely' is Ione's word for love; truest word last

event.ione_heart2.3.text: Two shells, tucked in the fold. Set aside, you might say. Nobody ever came back for them.
event.ione_heart2.3.why: quietly plants her set-aside motif six hearts before the shelf

event.ione_heart2.2.text: Take them. My best plan was to catalog them under S. I suspect the sea would object.
event.ione_heart2.2.why: sharper librarian joke; the sea gets the last word

event.ione_heart2.4.text: One cove has no name; the ink stops just short. I'd like to see it in winter. There. I've said it.
event.ione_heart2.4.why: she finally says the thing she'd never say, and marks that she said it

event.ione_heart5.0.text: I have a question for you. I wrote it down last Tuesday so I'd only have to be brave once.
event.ione_heart5.0.why: a day of the week, and the real confession: bravery is rationed

event.ione_heart5.3.text: The slip has vanished into Poetry, which serves me right. ...No matter. I know it by heart.
event.ione_heart5.3.why: 'by heart' lands the pun the scene is about

event.ione_heart5.2.text: Oh. Good. Then this is yours. A winter shore gave it to me years ago. I've kept it filed under someday.
event.ione_heart5.2.why: 'filed under someday' says the drawer, the waiting, and the hope in four words

event.reading_night.4.text: A snowdrop, for the lamp. ...Every chair taken. Next time, one more chair, and the door left open.
event.reading_night.4.why: fixes the chair count (the Wren branch already seats five); same open-door thread

event.ione_heart8.intro.text: Come with me, if you have a minute. There's a shelf at the back. I've shown nobody, not even Hazel. It's a little sad. It's mine.
event.ione_heart8.intro.why: 'not even Hazel' tells the player exactly how private this is

dlg.ione.shelf.0.text: A tall shelf stands at the back, apart from the rest. A slip of paper waits in every book. Each slip holds a date, and nothing else.
dlg.ione.shelf.0.why: dates instead of nothing: the paper remembers when, Ione remembers whom

dlg.ione.shelf.1.text: Every book set aside for somebody who never came. The oldest has waited nine years. Reshelving one would be deciding. What would you do?
dlg.ione.shelf.1.why: 'would be deciding' says why she can't, without explaining her feelings

dlg.ione.shelf.r1.text: Aloud? None of them has ever been heard. Go slowly, please. Nine years is a long time to wait for a voice.
dlg.ione.shelf.r1.why: calls back the nine years; clearer than 'they'll want to keep up'

dlg.ione.birthday.0.text: The new book can wait. Books are the only patient birthday guests. What shall we do?
dlg.ione.birthday.0.why: same patience joke, now with a party in it

event.ione_courtship2.intro.text: You asked for time. The question sat by the desk bell, and I dusted around it. Well. Would you court me?
event.ione_courtship2.intro.why: 'dusted around it' shows a year of care without a word of reproach

dlg.ione.partners.r2.text: The shore, with you. I won't even bring a book. Hazel will ask who I am.
dlg.ione.partners.r2.why: old line repeated my shipped festival joke; this one escalates instead

event.ione_partners.after.text: {if choice:courtship.ione.letter}The letter's in my favorite book now, marking the best page. Both are yours, eventually.{else}{if choice:courtship.ione.read}Your voice, my library. I've marked the spot where you stood. Nobody else may stand there. Hazel may.{else}The shore was bright, and I was bookless the whole time. ...I'd like to see it in winter. With you.{/if}{/if}
event.ione_partners.after.why: walk branch matched to the new r2 (no book brought); other branches kept

event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l4.text: Agreed. Tea, then. I'll stir it quietly, out of respect.
event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l4.why: respect for the quiet they just divided; funnier word last

event.overheard_hazel_ione_2.l1.text: Seven years overdue, this one on the desk. The card says Hazel. I'm not scolding. I'm admiring.
event.overheard_hazel_ione_2.l1.why: she never scolds, and now says so; sets up Hazel's last chapter

event.overheard_hazel_ione_3.l1.text: I put a chair by the window. It has a cushion. It's for nobody in particular.
event.overheard_hazel_ione_3.l1.why: 'nobody in particular' is more obviously for Hazel than 'whoever needs it'

event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l4.text: Then we both go home on time. Starting tomorrow. Possibly Thursday.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l4.why: the amendment admits neither of them will; specific day, funniest last

threads.ione_heart2: A cove with no name, where the chart's ink stops: Ione has finally said she wants to see it in winter.
threads.ione_heart5: Three low tides circled in ink in the almanac: which evening will the beach walk be?
threads.reading_night: One more chair and the door left open next time: who else will come to a reading night?
threads.festival_winter_lanterns: Ione's lantern drifted toward the sea and she claims she didn't steer it; the wish stays folded.
threads.ione_heart8: Slips with dates and no names, the oldest nine years old: who were the set-aside books waiting for?
threads.ione_birthday: The new book stays shut until noon, and something set aside for the player waits on the desk.
threads.ione_courtship: Sunday, the first page of a new book read aloud; or a question kept by the desk bell.
threads.ione_courtship2: The question keeps its place by the desk bell; waiting is most of a librarian's job.
threads.ione_partners: The winter shore, together: the thing Ione never asked anyone for now has a season attached.
threads.overheard_hazel_ione_1: The library's quiet belongs to Hazel and Ione only dusts it; the split stands, stirred quietly.
threads.overheard_odalys_ione_1: Two lamps lit past closing and a truce to go home on time, starting tomorrow, possibly Thursday.
threads.overheard_odalys_ione_2: Dr. Penn owes one chapter and a hand-delivered return; the returns box is sticky again.
threads.overheard_odalys_ione_3: Tea gone deliberately cold between the clinic and the library; the slow part is still working.

notes: Fixed a count: event.reading_night.4 said 'a fifth chair', but the Wren branch of event.reading_night.0 already seats five. Now 'one more chair', which works in both branches.
dlg.ione.partners.r2 repeated my shipped festival joke ('bring a book and not read it'); replaced it, and matched the walk branch of event.ione_partners.after so no book comes to the shore.

dlg.ione.shelf.0: the set-aside slips now carry a date and nothing else (before: blank). Keeps the shipped named slip on the desk distinct, makes 'nine years' visible, and lets any slip be tied to a villager later without naming one now.
